articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran Sanctions, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, and Amends General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.

In addition to the designations and removals, OFAC issued new general licenses pertaining to Iran and Russia. The agency also published amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these changes.
These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions policy across multiple regions, impacting various entities and transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
Accompanying these designations, OFAC also issued associated general licenses to guide compliance and authorized transactions.
These actions aim to combat intellectual property theft and protect American innovation through the application of targeted sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-related General License and FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License on October 16, 2026.
This amendment is accompanied by an updated Frequently Asked Question, providing clarification and guidance on the scope of authorized activities.
The changes are part of OFAC's ongoing adjustments to its Venezuela sanctions program, potentially impacting certain humanitarian or other authorized transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian and Cuban Entities, Issues New General Licenses

These actions are accompanied by the issuance of new and amended general licenses, along with updated Frequently Asked Questions, to provide guidance on the scope of the sanctions.
The designations target specific entities and individuals, aiming to further restrict financial activities related to Iran and Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuela-related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of a Venezuela-related designation on October 14, 2026.
This action signifies a change in the sanctions status for the previously designated individual or entity.
Such removals can indicate shifts in U.S. foreign policy or a determination that the designated party no longer meets the criteria for sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism designations on October 13, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and terrorist financing activities.
The action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting global criminal and terrorist networks through financial sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026.
This general license authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the Russia sanctions program.
The issuance of such licenses often aims to facilitate specific humanitarian activities, wind-down periods, or other limited engagements deemed permissible by OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities, Amends Russia-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 8, 2026.
In conjunction with these actions, OFAC also issued a new Iran-related General License and an amended Russia-related General License.
These measures reflect ongoing efforts to target Iran's financial networks while also making adjustments to the Russia sanctions program.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11.6 Million Over Sanctions Violations

This penalty is part of a coordinated enforcement action that also saw significant fines from FinCEN and the OCC for BSA/AML deficiencies.

articles.headline: Houthi Rebels Launch New Attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Aden
body: Houthi fighters have launched a series of attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia and the seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government in Aden.
Missiles reportedly struck Aden's airport and a coastguard base, marking the fourth such attack on Aden International Airport this month.
The attacks come as fighting intensifies around the city of Taiz, and Saudi air defenses have intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles and drones near Mecca.

articles.headline: Israeli Forces Intensify West Bank Operation, Displacing Hundreds in Hebron
body: The Israeli military is continuing a massive operation in the occupied West Bank, displacing hundreds of Palestinians and imposing significant movement restrictions.

In Hebron, Israeli forces have reportedly turned Palestinian homes into barracks and observation posts after forcing residents to leave, following a gun attack last week that killed two Israeli soldiers.
Since Friday, at least 47 Palestinians have been detained across Hebron, and 293 families, comprising about 2,200 people, have been forcibly displaced.

articles.headline: Clashes Erupt in France Amid Nationwide Protests Over Schools and Living Costs
body: Thousands of students and workers marched in Paris and other French cities on Saturday to protest school funding and soaring living costs.
Police used tear gas against demonstrators in Lyon and Clermont-Ferrand, where rallies were banned, as protests that began last month over staff shortages have grown into a national movement.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced that up to 70,000 officers would be deployed nationwide, as President Emmanuel Macron's popularity reaches its lowest point since taking office.

articles.headline: Ukraine Disputes Elon Musk's Claim of Starlink Terms of Service Violation
body: Ukrainian officials have disputed claims by SpaceX CEO Elon Musk that the country's military violated Starlink's terms of service by using the civilian satellite internet network for offensive drone strikes.
Musk stated on X that Ukraine's armed forces had 'violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people,' and that the 'loophole was closed last week.'

Ukrainian defense technology adviser Serhii Beskrestnov countered that long-standing restrictions on the civilian system in Ukraine made such offensive use impossible, and that full access to Starlink and the military-focused Starshield service was restored on Saturday.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026, Including Penalties Against Major Banks
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, including a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program.

The OCC also assessed a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, National Association, for deficiencies in its BSA compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and sending wires with inaccurate transmittor name information.

Additionally, the OCC issued Orders of Prohibition against two institution-affiliated parties for embezzling customer funds: Jennifer Hamblin of Fifth Third Bank, N.A., for approximately $292,000, and Christopher Organista of U.S. Bank National Association, for approximately $194,131.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
